sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Franklin County
sections.html:
Three units make up the Franklin County Tax Office: Assessor's Office, Collections Department and GIS/Mapping. Phone 919-496-2172 for any of them, and expect voicemail at busy times.

  • Assessor: this desk lists and values land, buildings, business and personal property, and registered vehicles. Value questions go to Tax Assessor's Office, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549.
  • Collections: enforces the Machinery Act on current and past due accounts. Mail payments and certification requests to Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549.
  • GIS/Mapping: keeps the parcel layer for the county.

September 1 is the due date. Bills for 2026 go delinquent on January 6, 2027.

The county prints statements around late July or early August. A payment that arrives before September 1 earns a discount, and prepaying before the bill run is allowed. Once a bill is delinquent, collection becomes forceful, and G.S. 105-360 adds interest of 2 percent through February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for every later month or fraction of a month.

BIS Online Services, a third party, handles cards and charges a non-refundable convenience fee. Its phone line is 877-768-4775. Keep the tax year, bill number, local zip code and amount in front of you, and ring the county office at 919-496-2172 to get the amount. Mail can cross a past-due notice, so pay early and add interest if you are late.

Sellers: before you pick a closing date, get a current balance from the Collections Department.

sections.h2: If your lender escrows the tax
sections.html:
Escrow does not stop the mailing. Every bill still goes to the owner of record, and lenders take the ones they owe from a file the county supplies.

You can check that your lender paid by searching the county collection site during the second week of September or by calling 919-496-2172 and pressing option 2. It also helps to send the mortgage company a copy of the bill with your next payment. Already sold? Pass the bill to the new owner unless you plan to pay it. Deals between buyers, sellers and attorneys are not the county's business, but the tax is a lien, so a buyer will want every bill cleared at closing.

Franklin County's Register of Deeds has turned away transfer deeds since April 1, 2015, unless the Tax Collector has first certified that no delinquent tax lien sits on the parcel.

There is no charge. Collections offers the service on weekdays in business hours and shuts for county holidays. Your closing attorney or you can drop in before recording. By mail, address the envelope to the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, and add Attention: Tax Certification. Electronic filings go through the step on their own.

Any open bill can stall the sale. Pay it yourself, or have the closing agent pay from your proceeds so the certificate gets issued.

Real estate appeals can be filed from January 1 until the county board of review adjourns, which is usually in May. If you receive a notice of changed value, a separate 30-day clock begins.

The January 1, 2024 revaluation sets current values. The county asks that you send the finished appeal form plus every supporting paper to Franklin County Revaluation, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549, ahead of April. Staff look at it first. Whatever they cannot resolve gets a board hearing and a mailed decision. A filing that misses adjournment waits for the next tax year. Beyond the board sits the state Property Tax Commission, which needs notice within 30 days, and the owner must show a substantial overstatement.

Which appeal reasons the county accepts
Reason offeredCounty position
Bill is higher than before, or income is fixed in retirementNo legal basis
Prices fell or you paid less after January 1, 2024No legal basis under G.S. 105-287
Similar homes carry lower assessed valuesHas a legal basis
Highly similar sales before January 1, 2024 at far lower pricesHas a legal basis
Fire, wind or water damage still unrepaired on January 1Has a legal basis, with proof and photos
Septic permit denied, with a Health Department letterHas a legal basis

sections.h2: Relief for owners on a fixed income
sections.html:
The state offers three programs, but you may use just one: the senior or disability exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion or the circuit breaker cap.

  • An owner who is elderly or disabled and earns no more than the 2026 ceiling of $38,800 excludes $25,000 of value, or half the value where that is greater.
  • A veteran with a qualifying disability excludes $45,000 of value, and age and income do not matter.
  • The circuit breaker requires five or more years of ownership. Tax is capped at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent where income is $38,800 up to $58,200, with the excess deferred.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor instead of the state revenue department. Income does not reduce the value itself, so a retiree with relief questions should phone the Tax Assessor's Office. Selling the home makes any circuit breaker deferral payable.

sections.h2: Solid waste fee and tax liens
sections.html:
A solid waste availability fee rides on bills for any dwelling or business with an electrical hookup, and the tax is a lien on the parcel.

Money from the fee pays for trash pickup and disposal at twelve convenience centers. Each electrical connection is charged, even when nobody lives in the house full time, which means an empty house with power still owes it. The commissioners set a new amount every year in the budget ordinance, so call the Tax Office for your parcel's figure.

When a bill stays unpaid, the lien dates back to the listing date under G.S. 105-355. The county may then foreclose in court under G.S. 105-374, with a sale at the courthouse door and a 10-day period for higher bids. Someone in bankruptcy still receives bills, but the collector cannot chase delinquent tax while the case is open.

sections.h2: Selling with back taxes or an inherited house
sections.html:
An inherited house carries the same lien. The tax collector can tell you which years are open. Before the court confirms a foreclosure sale, a person redeeming under G.S. 105-374 pays taxes, penalties, interest and costs to clear the debt.

  1. Call Collections for the unpaid years and a payoff figure.
  2. Get the certification stamped before the deed is taken to the Register of Deeds.
  3. Let the closing agent settle the balance out of what you receive.

Selling for cash does not remove any of this. Every transfer needs the lien cleared and the certificate issued.

Growth defines the county. Population reached 82,037 by mid-2025, compared with 68,625 in 2020, spread over 491.80 square miles of land. Homeowners live in 78.6 percent of occupied housing, and the median owner-occupied value is $284,300.

faqs.q: On what date do 2026 Franklin County bills go delinquent?
faqs.a: January 6, 2027, after the September 1 due date.

faqs.q: Will Franklin County record my deed without a tax certification?
faqs.a: No, a real property transfer needs the Tax Collector to certify first that no delinquent lien exists. The stamp is free during weekday office hours.

faqs.q: Where does a Franklin County value appeal go?
faqs.a: Send the form and your papers to P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549. You can file from January 1 until the board adjourns, or for 30 days after a changed value notice.

faqs.q: Does a larger bill justify a lower Franklin County value?
faqs.a: No. A bigger bill or a fixed income is not a legal reason. Better evidence is lower values on similar properties, sales from before 2024 or documented damage.

faqs.q: What number do I use to check or pay a Franklin County bill?
faqs.a: To check payments, dial 919-496-2172 and press option 2. To pay by card over the phone, call BIS Online Services at 877-768-4775 and expect a convenience fee.
